subject: Follow-up: GPU package and token economics — throughput & budget
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Max Liu <max@elliot.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@elliot.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: GPU package and token economics — throughput & budget

Hi Max — great talking earlier. Quick recap + two asks so we can size a dedicated package that fits Elliot.ai's performance and budget targets.

Summary from call:
- Current usage: ~18M requests/month, average prompt+response ~350 tokens, roughly 6.3B tokens/month (customer-provided snapshot attached).
- Target production latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for short prompts (~<512 tokens).
- Throughput requirement: steady-state 120 concurrent requests (p99 peak ~180) translating to ~60–80 tokens/sec sustained per model instance depending on sequence distribution.
- Preferred models: evaluator mentioned Llama-3 style base; we recommended testing 13B and 70B variants for quality/throughput tradeoffs.

Budget and unit economics discussed:
- Elliot.ai target unit price: $8–$12 per 1M tokens (target $/1M = $10).
- Monthly budget band: $12k–$25k initially for inference (excludes storage/ingress).
- Willingness to commit: 6–12 month reserved term if unit economics and SLA align.

Sizing options (high-level):
1) H100-80GB fleet (high throughput): 3x GPUs reserved — estimated baseline capacity ~1.8B tokens/day (burst capable). Estimated unit cost to Elliot w/ 12mo commitment: ~$9.5 per 1M tokens.
2) A100-80GB balanced option: 4x GPUs reserved — lower peak but lower monthly commitment: estimated ~$11.2 per 1M tokens.
3) Mixed lane (1 H100 + 2 A100) — fallback routing to cheaper lanes for non-low-latency requests; estimated ~$10.1 per 1M tokens.

Two asks before we turn this into a formal proposal/PoC:
1) Confirm a realistic monthly token burn scenario (conservative / expected / optimistic) — the attached elliot_usage_snapshot.csv helps but we'd like a 2-week representative export (UTC timestamps).
2) Confirm whether procurement prefers a single line item (per-GPU reserved lanes) or a fixed monthly all-in price. If procurement needs an SOW, loop them in and we’ll draft a committed SKU + SLA appendix.

Next steps I propose this week:
- I’ll draft an initial SKU matrix (3 options above with token econs and latency SLOs) and share a DocuSign-enabled proposal for a 30-day pilot.
- You share a 2-week usage export and confirm procurement contact.

Attachments: elliot_usage_snapshot.csv, quick-sku-estimates.xlsx (see attached filenames).

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Max Liu <max@elliot.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GPU package and token economics — throughput & budget

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the clear write-up. Quick responses inline:

> Current usage: ~18M requests/month…
We can provide a trimmed export from our telemetry system; I’ll have our infra team send a 14-day sample by EOD Thursday.

> Target unit price: $8–$12 per 1M tokens…
That range is fine as a target — procurement will push back on anything above $10/1M without strong SLA guarantees. If you can show a 30-day pilot at ~$9.5/1M that converts to a committed plan, that would be compelling.

> Sizing options
We like the H100 option for latency but need certainty around cold-cache p95s. Also, can you confirm how automatic fallback to cheaper lanes would affect request routing (we need consistent latency for our critical path).

Procurement contact: procurement@elliot.ai (CC’ing Raj Patel). Raj — can you confirm whether you prefer committed SKUs or an all-in monthly line item for budgeting?

—Max
Max Liu
Head of Platform, Elliot.ai
max@elliot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GPU package and token economics — throughput & budget

Sofia / Sean — quick internal note:
- If Elliot can sign a 12mo committed plan we can move the H100 option to $8.9/1M (with a 30-day pilot at $9.2/1M). That concession requires a 30% minimum monthly throughput guarantee and a single-point SLA escalation (enterprise support).
- For the fallback routing ask: operations needs to add a per-route pinning flag so critical paths never route off the low-latency lane. Make sure to call that out in the proposal.

Suggested next steps for the external doc:
1) Provide the 30-day SKU matrix as Sofia drafted, include explicit per-token math (tokens/day -> tokens/month -> implied cost).
2) Add an appendix on routing behavior & pinning for critical routes.
3) Attach the DocuSign link and set pilot start window as 7/20–7/27.

I’ll pre-approve the price band if procurement confirms the 12mo term.
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Max Liu <max@elliot.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@elliot.ai>, procurement@elliot.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GPU package and token economics — throughput & budget

Thanks Raj / Max — looping in our ops + legal quietly once procurement confirms preferred contract structure. Action items we’ll own:
- I’ll upload the SKU matrix (H100 / A100 / mixed) with per-token math and latency SLOs to the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign proposal link by EOD Friday. (HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567890)
- Operations: add note about route pinning for critical endpoints; we’ll include an appendix describing deterministic routing for pinned routes.
- Pilot window: tentatively 7/20 start, 30-day duration; pilot pricing will be $9.2/1M for H100 option if Elliot agrees to a 12mo conversion.

Please confirm the 14-day usage export ETA and whether procurement prefers committed SKUs vs one-line monthly. If you confirm now I’ll draft the DocuSign SOW and share the link.

Best —
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
